item.title: Ted Cruz calls El-Sayed a "jihadist leprechaun" at campaign stop
item.description: At a campaign event outside of Detroit, GOP Sen. Ted Cruz of Texas attempted to tie Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed to the Muslim Brotherhood.

item.description: The Iran war looms over the midterm elections as costs mount and gas prices squeeze voters' wallets. CBS News' Weijia Jiang has more on this, plus Lana Zak reports on races in Iowa.

item.description: Missing pages and a reference to classified documents contradict the Justice Department's claims about the Epstein files.

item.title: Labor activist Dolores Huerta says Trump "does not know history"

item.title: Dolores Huerta speaks out in first public interview since Chavez assault claims
item.description: In her first public interview since the investigation, Dolores Huerta said that at the time of the incidents, she felt alone and trapped.

item.title: Dolores Huerta says Cesar Chavez "manipulated and pressured" her as abuse allegations emerge
item.description: Dolores Huerta, who co-founded the United Farm Workers movement with Cesar Chavez, alleges that Chavez "manipulated and pressured" and later forced her against her will to have sex with him in the 1960s, fathering two children. She spoke out after two other women alleged to The New York Times that they were sexually abused by Chavez in the 1970s when they were 12 and 13 years old.

item.title: Dolores Huerta alleges assault by Cesar Chavez amid abuse claims
item.description: Allegations of abuse of women and girls by union leader Cesar Chavez were first reported by the New York Times​ on Wednesday.

item.title: Note to Self: Dolores Huerta looks back on her fight for farm workers' rights
item.description: During Hispanic Heritage Month, labor activist Dolores Huerta reflects on her fight for farm workers' rights alongside Cesar Chavez in the 1960s and her ongoing work to help others.

item.title: Dolores Huerta turns 94. Here's a look at the civil rights icon's legacy.
item.description: She's considered one of the most respected and influential labor leaders of our time. Dolores Huerta broke more than a glass ceiling; she led a revolution in the farm fields of California's Central Valley.

item.title: Dolores Huerta's 50 years of activism
item.description: At 84, the woman President Obama stole his campaign slogan from — albeit in a different language — is still a giant in the fight against inequality
